name: AML/PLAFT compliance kit for small real estate agents, accountants and corporate-service providers (SENACLAFT)
buyer: Small estate agencies, property developers, accountants, lawyers on listed operations, corporate-service providers, and from 2026 non-financial trustees and professionals serving foreign activities
trigger: Ley 19.574 art. 13, Decreto 379/018: register with SENACLAFT, update data within 30 days, risk matrix, written risk analysis, customer due diligence, staff training, unusual-transaction reports. Ley 20.469 (19/03/2026) widened the subjects and extends controls to real estate deals paid in kind or with virtual assets; Res. 061/2026 makes non-registration a serious infringement. Notaries do not register (Caja Notarial supplies data).
evidence: https://www.gub.uy/tramites/inscripcion-sujetos-obligados-sector-no-financiero (fetched; registration literals and exemptions); https://www.ferrere.com/es/novedades/cambios-significativos-al-regimen-plaft/ (Ley 20.469 changes need updated matrices and manuals, regulation pending); RSM Uruguay note on Res. 061/2026
existing: Competitor search 'software prevencion lavado de activos inmobiliarias contadores Uruguay' found no Uruguay-specific tool, only law-firm notes; regional AML software exists but was not seen for this segment. Law firms and consultancies sell policy manuals.
unchecked: Whether regional vendors (e.g. generic PLAFT SaaS) target Uruguayan SMEs; number of registered subjects; actual SENACLAFT inspection intensity; whether the lack of periodic reports reduces recurring demand; reglamentacion of Ley 20.469 still pending.

first_check.duty: Ley 19.574 art. 13 (as amended by Ley 20.469, promulgated 19/03/2026 and published 10/04/2026) and Decreto 379/018 apply to real estate agencies, developers, builders, auctioneers, and to accountants and lawyers on listed operations. From Res. 54/2026 (12/05/2026) they also cover non-financial trustees and providers of administration, accounting or data services to clients abroad. These subjects must register with SENACLAFT, appoint a compliance officer, keep a risk matrix, assess each client and operation in writing (low, medium or high risk), run due diligence, find source of funds and beneficial owners, train staff, report unusual operations to the UIAF and keep records for 5 years. Ley 20.469 cuts the cash threshold to UI 200,000 (or 5% of the operation, capped at UI 450,000) and requires updated matrices and manuals, but its regulation is still pending. Res. 061/2026 replaces Res. 016/2022 and makes failure to register, update data or perform due diligence, and failure to identify beneficial owners, serious infringements. The frequency is per transaction plus continuous upkeep. No fixed periodic filing was found.
first_check.market: No count found. No public statistic gives the number of registered non-financial subjects (checked SENACLAFT news and law-firm notes). As a proxy, the non-financial sector filed only 107 suspicious-activity reports in 2025, against 973 from the financial sector (Presidencia, citing the UIAF annual report). The buyer pool probably runs to a few thousand real estate firms, builders, auctioneers, accountants and corporate-service providers in a country of about 3.5M people. This is an estimate, not verified.
first_check.competitor: No Uruguay-specific PLAFT SaaS for non-financial subjects turned up in 5 local-language searches. Existing options: Crowe Uruguay sells done-for-you PLAFT due-diligence reports for estate agents, auctioneers and notaries (delivered within 72 working hours); law firms and consultancies (Ferrere, RSM, PwC) sell manuals and advice; the UIAF/BCU publishes free control lists (PEPs, UN list, non-cooperating countries) but no workflow tool. Regional vendors from Argentina, Chile and Colombia were not seen targeting Uruguay; this was not exhaustively checked.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. Ley 19.574 art. 13 and Decreto 379/018 require subjects to register with SENACLAFT, appoint a compliance officer, keep a risk matrix, write a risk analysis per client and operation, run due diligence and keep records for 5 years. Ley 20.469 (published 10/04/2026) and Res. 54/2026 added new subjects. Res. 061/2026 treats non-registration and missing due diligence as serious infringements. I found no software built for Uruguayan non-financial subjects, only consultancy services (Crowe's per-client PLAFT reports) and the free UIAF control lists. Repeat use comes from per-transaction due diligence, but it is event-driven, not a periodic filing. The market is small and uncounted. Only 107 non-financial suspicious-activity reports in 2025 suggests weak enforcement. Rules for Ley 20.469 are still pending.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial substitutes: Crowe Uruguay's done-for-you PLAFT service, SENACLAFT's free sector guides with forms (form content unverified, PDF unreadable), the LUC simplification for electronic payments, and generic AML screening APIs such as Didit.
challenge_check.reason: Eight Spanish-language searches found no Uruguay-specific PLAFT SaaS for non-financial obliged subjects. The only things close to it are Crowe's done-for-you due-diligence reports for estate agents and auctioneers, manuals from law firms (Ferrere, RSM) and generic screening APIs (Didit). None of these kills the idea. It is weakened in three ways. SENACLAFT publishes free sector guides with standard forms; the guide text quotes an observations box on "the forms", but I could not open the PDF. Under Ley 19.889 (LUC), due diligence can be simplified when payment is electronic. And Uruguay is a small market whose size I could not find. Ley 20.469 added new subjects: Res. 54/2026 opened their registration (deadline 10/07/2026) and Res. 61/2026 set a new sanctions scale. These give fresh triggers, but SENACLAFT recorded only 50 sanctions in 2023, so enforcement is light.
